_comment: Seeded ONLY from forms an engine actually produced. Sources: two human takes of fixtures/dictation-script.md through Apple SpeechTranscriber and Parakeet TDT v3, plus the synthesised fixtures. Nothing here is invented — every 'spoken' entry was observed, with one kind of exception: a case_sensitive term fires only on an input written as one of its spoken forms or its written form (exactly, or a lower-case form with its first letter capitalised, as at the start of a sentence), so its written form in lower case ('ogham', 'terraform', ...) and the casings 'TerraForm' and 'cube c t l' are listed as case variants of wanted corrections, not as observed mishearings. 'om' is deliberately not listed: it is an ordinary word. 'azure' is an ordinary word too, but stays: Apple produced it for Azure, and its term has a 0.95 threshold. See docs/benchmarks.md.
_excluded_note: Deliberately NOT seeded, though observed: 'parcel'/'passer' -> parser (both are real words; correcting them would break 'send me the parcel'), 'PostgreSQL' -> Postgres (a legitimate alternative name, not a mishearing, and the user's own choice), and the homophones cash/cache and sink/sync (both spellings are ordinary English, so a rule breaks the other sense in the same sentence). These need engine biasing or user judgement, not a blanket rewrite.
